 Kane Williamson names next generation of ‘Fab Four’ batters 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 19 November 2026, 2:20 pm 
 3 min read
 19 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | Kane Williamson names next generation of ‘Fab Four’ batters 
 Former New Zealand cricketer Kane Williamson has identified Indian players Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal, fellow New Zealander Rachin Ravindra, England white-ball captain Harry Brook, and Australian all-rounder Cameron Green as the next generation of the ‘Fab Four’ in cricket batting.
 The term ‘Fab Four’ was coined in 2014 by former New Zealand cricketer Martin Crowe to describe Williamson, Indian batting star Virat Kohli, Australian Steve Smith, and English batsman Joe Root. These players were recognised as future leaders of their nations and prolific run-scorers. Over the subsequent years, they have established themselves as some of the greatest cricketers in the Test format, with Virat Kohli having amassed over 28,000 international runs and 86 centuries, securing his status as an all-format legend.

 In an interview with Nasser Hussain on The ICC Review, Williamson reflected on his inclusion in the ‘Fab Four’ and stated he never felt additional pressure as part of the group. “I never felt a burden with it,” he said. “I admired those other three that you mentioned of the ‘Fab Four’ and I know them all well having played with Rooty at Yorkshire and obviously against them for a long time. I really did admire them and love the way they go about it, and they are all very, very different.”
 Although recognising the significance of individual achievements and being mentioned alongside these cricket greats, Williamson emphasised his primary focus was always on supporting New Zealand and contributing to team success. “For me it was just it was always about what you can do for the team and how you keep doing more, and I did love the team focus because it’s also a great way to keep extending your game and that it’s never enough,” he explained. “That was where my focus was, and it was about just trying to make valuable contributions for the team. Yeah, rather than it is very difficult to just compare and measure, and it’s not a very fun thing to do, but it is also you just you are constantly playing in different conditions, you know, at different times, and so, yeah, it just kind of lands where it does.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Reflecting on their careers, Williamson added, “I never thought a lot about it when I played, but looking back since retiring, it is quite sort of unique in some ways. There are four of us that sort of hung around for a while and scored a few runs.”
 With Williamson and Kohli having retired from Test cricket and Smith and Root nearing the end of their careers, attention has turned to which players will form the next generation to create a new ‘Fab Four’ in Test cricket. When asked by Hussain, Williamson nominated five players he believes have the potential to elevate their game to such a level.
 He said, “I have answered this question before actually, so I would better say the same otherwise (it is) a bit of a fraud. But I had Harry Brook, I had Shubman Gill, I had Cameron Green, and I actually had Yashasvi Jaiswal too. And there was another one, but that was Rachin Ravindra. But I think maybe a challenge he might have is the volume of cricket and maybe Test cricket, because I do not know where that will land, but he would be in there for me too.”
